STEP 1 - Vessel type: square flat plate (white, rim band visible, flat centre, no inner wall).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Square plates are typically 20-30 cm. This one looks like a standard dinner size, so about 25 cm.
b) Reference: the bagel half is roughly 10-11 cm across (bread slice-sized). The plate spans about 2.2-2.4 bagel widths across the long side, giving roughly 24-26 cm.
Reconciled width: 25 cm. Area = 625 cm².

STEP 3 - Items:
- Hash browns: spread over about 15% of the plate, roughly 94 cm². Thin shredded layer, about 1.5 cm average (2 cm peak). Volume ≈ 94 × 1.5 = 141 ml. Density for mixed potato/fried ~0.6 → about 85 g.
- Scrambled eggs with orange/red sauce (hot sauce or ketchup-like): about 20% of plate, 125 cm². Mound about 2 cm average. Volume ≈ 250 ml × 0.8 = 200 g.
- Bagel half (whole-grain, cream cheese spread): bagel half is about 10 cm diameter, area ≈ 79 cm², thickness about 1.5 cm (bread slice-type), volume ≈ 118 ml × 0.3 = 35 g of bagel. Cream cheese smear covering most of the top, ~0.3-0.5 cm thick over ~60 cm² ≈ 25 ml × 1.0 ≈ 25 g.
- Cantaloupe/honeydew-style melon chunks (pale green): about 4 pieces, roughly 3 × 3 × 2.5 cm each ≈ 22 ml each, about 90 ml total × 0.6 ≈ 55 g. Visible pieces are close to 60 g; use 60 g.

Total food ≈ 85 + 200 + 35 + 25 + 60 = 405 g.

STEP 4 - No hidden base layer beyond what is visible; the plate is mostly sparsely loaded, so the total stays in the low-hundreds range.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g (as served):
- Hash browns, fried: ~230 kcal/100 g
- Scrambled eggs with butter/oil: ~170 kcal/100 g
- Whole-grain bagel: ~250 kcal/100 g
- Cream cheese: ~340 kcal/100 g (used for the spread)
- Melon: ~35 kcal/100 g

Energy check: hash browns 85 g ≈ 196 kcal; eggs 200 g ≈ 340 kcal; bagel 35 g ≈ 88 kcal; cream cheese 25 g ≈ 85 kcal; melon 60 g ≈ 21 kcal. Total ≈ 730 kcal.
